key_insight: ActMOF creates an experiment-grounded benchmark to compare active-learning strategies for MOF synthesis and shows Gaussian-process-based search is among the strongest in sparse crystallization spaces.
engineering_relevance: It gives materials engineers a reusable testbed for choosing synthesis optimizers that can reduce experimental trial count while improving the odds of obtaining crystalline MOFs.
method: Emulated a MOF synthesis landscape from measured microwave experiments.
Assigned each condition a crystallinity index from diffraction peak intensity and peak width.
Benchmarked GP, tree-ensemble, and LLM-guided policies for active learning.
evidence_signal: The benchmark identified GP-family policies as leading performers and then transferred the strategy to six related aluminum MOF syntheses, each yielding crystalline products within 12 experiments.
watch_item: Results are tied to a specific aluminum-carboxylate, microwave-synthesis setting, so broader transfer to other chemistries or noise regimes still needs validation.
paper_title: ActMOF: Mapping Reticular Synthesis through Active Learning
